sections.strategy: Asda confirmed (Retail Gazette, 21 Sept) that the Rotherham Parkgate Asda Living unit reopens as a standalone George concept store on Thursday 1 October, the last standalone opening planned for 2026, after Peterborough, Lincoln, Maidstone and Barnsley. Asda repeated its target of 100 standalone George stores over five years and describes George as the UK's third-largest clothing retailer by volume and its largest childrenswear retailer. The planned move of George.com fulfilment to DHL Derby from January 2027 is still on track, backing Asda's forecast that George.com will double in size by 2032.
sections.pricing: The AW26 womenswear hero range runs from £8 for essentials to £45 for statement outerwear. The Micah Richards menswear capsule, launched 14 Sept, runs from £12 (supima cotton tee) to £50 (faux-leather jacket). Both sit above Primark's entry prices while still being sold as 'high-end fashion at high-street value'. We found no new price moves against Primark, Tu or F&F this week.
sections.launches: Trade press (FashionNetwork, 22 Sept) covered George's 'biggest autumn womenswear campaign in years'. Created by Lucky Generals and styled by Sinead McKeefry, it features statement jackets, quilted paisley, western-tinged checks and relaxed denim, and runs across VOD, social 'Style Stories' and OOH. It also includes a George x Grazia magazine and DOOH tie-in for London Fashion Week. The Micah Richards menswear capsule (tailoring, textured overshirts, olive/chocolate/taupe/stone palette) is still being pushed in stores and will be stocked at the new Rotherham store.
sections.gossip: Industry backdrop, not George-specific: the CBI Distributive Trades Survey (25 Sept) showed UK retail orders to suppliers falling at the fastest rate on record (-62, down from -29 in August), with sales at -55 and orders expected to fall further to -63 in October. GMB's earlier claim that the DHL outsourcing 'paves the way for a full carve-up' of Asda under TDR Capital is still being talked about in the trade.
soWhat: The CBI's record fall in retailer orders is the biggest risk this week. Even though George is growing, expect tighter AW26 repeats and SS27 commitments and more pressure on cost prices. Protect margin by pushing for firm order volumes before agreeing price concessions.

George is spending on trend-led womenswear (paisley quilting, checks, western denim) and elevated menswear basics (supima cotton, textured overshirting). Suppliers who can offer premium-feel fabrics at an £8–£50 retail price have the strongest pitch for SS27 range reviews.

Sourcing, vendor and sustainability news has now been quiet for several weeks. Proactively ask George's sourcing team, or PDS 'Sourcing as a Service', about SS27 capacity plans and any post-2025 George for Good fibre targets, since the 2025 commitments have lapsed and no replacements have been published.
